CodeTerminal

CodeTerminal reads the ANSI codes that test runners and package managers print: bold, dim, italic, underline, the 16 colours mapped to theme tokens that read well in light and dark, 256 colours and truecolor. Carriage returns overwrite the line, so progress bars and spinners settle on their last state, OSC 8 links become real links, and a code split across two chunks never flashes on screen. Copy gives plain text, and long output folds behind “Show all”.

Highlighting uses Shiki with GitHub’s light and dark themes, loaded per language on demand. Only new lines are tokenized as text arrives, so long files stay fast, and both themes render at once so switching color scheme never flashes. Blocks longer than 16 lines fold behind “Show all”.

In CodeTerminal the header status is announced, “Running” and then “Exited with code 1”, links from the output say they open in a new tab, and colours from the output are theme tokens with readable contrast in light and dark.
